{{technical|date=March 2017}}

In [[mathematics]] and [[supersymmetric gauge theory]], '''spectral networks''' are "networks of [[Trajectory|trajectories]] on [[Riemann surface]]s obeying certain local rules. Spectral networks arise naturally in [[Four-dimensional space|four-dimensional]] ''N''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 theories coupled to surface defects, particularly the theories of class S."<ref>{{Cite journal|arxiv=1204.4824|title= Spectral networks|journal= Annales Henri Poincaré|volume= 14|issue= 7|pages= 1643|last1= Gaiotto|first1= Davide|last2=  Moore|first2= Gregory W.|last3= Neitzke|first3= Andrew|year= 2012|doi= 10.1007/s00023-013-0239-7|bibcode= 2013AnHP...14.1643G|s2cid= 118723363}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| title=Spectral Networks and Their Applications | url=http://hep.caltech.edu/ym35/presentations/Moore.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304082228/http://hep.caltech.edu/ym35/presentations/Moore.pdf | archive-date=2016-03-04}}</ref>
